# Introduction and study context {#sec-intro}

On 1 February 2021 the Myanmar military removed the elected National League for Democracy government
and formed the State Administration Council. Security forces killed more than six hundred protesters
in the following months (Council on Foreign Relations, 2026). The first armed resistance by
protesters was recorded in Kalay, Sagaing Region, on 28 March 2021. Armed resistance in Mindat, Chin
State, began on 26 April 2021. The National Unity Government announced its People's Defence Force on
5 May 2021 (Wikipedia, "Myanmar conflict").

Before the coup, armed conflict in Myanmar was concentrated in the ethnic states along the land
borders, where ethnic armed organisations have fought the military since independence in 1948
(Wikipedia, "Myanmar conflict"). Since the coup, fighting has been recorded in at least 321 of the
country's 330 townships, including the Bamar-majority regions of central Myanmar, where little
fighting was recorded in the decades before 2021 (Su Mon, 2024). More than 2,600 new non-state armed
groups have been recorded since April 2021 (Su Mon, 2024). The newer groups use drones, improvised
explosives and ambushes. The military uses airstrikes and ground assaults on villages (Su Mon,
2024).

Ethnic self-determination, competition between armed groups over territory and resources, and
opposition to the coup all drive the fighting, in different combinations in different areas (Su Mon,
2024; Wikipedia, "Myanmar conflict"). Armed conflict events are mapped here over the 57 months of
the study period, to show where they concentrate, which townships differ from their neighbours, and
how the spatial pattern changed.

The 87,109 event records of the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED) for Myanmar,
from 1 January 2021 to 30 September 2025, were aggregated to the 330 townships of the Myanmar
Information Management Unit (MIMU) boundary layer, version 9.4.

# Research questions and objectives {#sec-question}

| Objective | Research question | Method |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Pinpoint hot spots, cold spots and spatial outliers of violence | **RQ1.** Which townships belong to clusters of high or low counts of armed conflict events, and which differ from their neighbours, at p < 0.05? | Local measures of spatial association: local Moran's I, local Geary's c, Getis-Ord Gi and Gi* (@sec-lmsa) |
| Reveal where, how fast and in what pattern violence evolved | **RQ2.** Where did hot and cold spots of armed conflict events emerge, intensify, persist or fade between 2021 and 2025? | Emerging hot spot analysis on a space-time cube (@sec-ehsa) |

RQ3 and RQ4 extend the objectives of the exercise:

- **RQ3.** Do the three event types (battles; explosions and remote violence; violence against
  civilians) concentrate in the same townships? (@sec-lmsa-types)
- **RQ4.** Did the local Moran's I clusters of armed conflict events change after the Operation 1027
  offensive began on 27 October 2023? (@sec-value-added)

# Data and study design {#sec-data}

## Software and packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| code-fold: true
pacman::p_load(sf, sfdep, spdep, tmap, tidyverse, seastests, Kendall, modifiedmk, ggrepel,
               knitr, kableExtra, patchwork)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
`p_load()` loads the packages and installs any that are missing: **sf** for the vector data,
**sfdep** and **spdep** for neighbours, weights and the spatial statistics, **tmap** and
**tidyverse** (ggplot2) for maps and charts, **seastests**, **Kendall** and **modifiedmk** for the
seasonality and trend tests, and **knitr**, **kableExtra**, **ggrepel** and **patchwork** for
tables, labels and layouts.
:::

## Sources

| Dataset | Source | Content | Licence |
|--------|------------------------------------------|----------------------------|---------------------|
| ACLED events, Myanmar | ACLED, provided on eLearn | 87,109 events, 1 Jan 2021 to 30 Sep 2025, 31 fields | ACLED terms of use; kept out of the public repository |
| Township boundaries | MIMU GeoNode, layer `mmr_polbnda_adm3_250k_mimu_1`, "Myanmar Township Boundaries MIMU v9.4" (18 Jun 2023) | 330 townships, EPSG:4326, digitised at 1:250,000 | Free with attribution |
| Township population | OCHA, Common Operational Dataset on Population Statistics, `mmr_admpop_adm3_2023.csv` | Department of Population projection for 2023, based on the 2014 census | CC BY |

```{r}
#| label: import
#| code-fold: true
acled <- read_csv("data/aspatial/ACLED_Data_Myanmar_Jan2021-Sep2025.csv") |>
  mutate(event_date = as.Date(event_date))

tsp <- st_read("data/geospatial/mmr_polbnda_adm3_250k_mimu_1.shp", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(32647) |>
  arrange(TS_PCODE)

pop <- read_csv("data/aspatial/mmr_admpop_adm3_2023.csv") |>
  select(TS_PCODE = ADM3_PCODE, pop = T_TL)
```

```{r}
#| label: gg-key
#| code-fold: true
# north arrow and scale bar for the ggplot maps, in the style of tm_compass() and tm_scalebar()
gg_key <- function(x, y, u, km = 200, north = NULL, at = NULL) {
  add <- \(d) if (is.null(at)) d else cbind(d, at[rep(1, nrow(d)), , drop = FALSE])
  bar <- add(data.frame(xmin = x, xmax = x + km * 1000, ymin = y, ymax = y + 0.012 * u))
  lab <- add(data.frame(x = c(x, x + km * 1000), y = y - 0.022 * u,
                        key_txt = c("0", paste(km, "km"))))
  out <- list(
    geom_rect(data = bar, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
              fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4, inherit.aes = FALSE),
    geom_text(data = lab, aes(x, y, label = key_txt), size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE))
  if (!is.null(north)) {
    cx <- north[1]; by <- north[2]; ty <- by + 0.075 * u; hw <- 0.016 * u; ny <- by + 0.02 * u
    half <- \(sx) add(data.frame(x = c(cx, cx + sx * hw, cx), y = c(ty, by, ny)))
    out <- c(out, list(
      geom_polygon(data = half(-1), aes(x, y), fill = "white", colour = "black",
                   linewidth = 0.4, inherit.aes = FALSE),
      geom_polygon(data = half(1), aes(x, y), fill = "black", colour = "black",
                   linewidth = 0.4, inherit.aes = FALSE),
      geom_text(data = add(data.frame(x = cx, y = ty + 0.025 * u)), aes(x, y), label = "N",
                size = 3.4, inherit.aes = FALSE)))
  }
  out
}
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
`read_csv()` and `st_read()` read the events and the township layer. `st_transform(32647)` projects
the townships to UTM zone 47N, so that distances are in metres. `arrange(TS_PCODE)` sorts the townships, because `emerging_hotspot_analysis()` assigns its
results by row order (@sec-ehsa). `select(TS_PCODE = ADM3_PCODE, pop = T_TL)` keeps two population
columns under new names (`new_name = old_name`).

Myanmar spans 92.2°E to 101.2°E, across UTM zones 46N (90°E to 96°E) and 47N (96°E to 102°E). Zone
47N is used for the whole country because its central meridian, 99°E, is at most 6.8° from any part
of Myanmar, against 8.2° for the central meridian of zone 46N, 93°E:

```{r}
#| label: utm-zones
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 6
zn_ts <- st_transform(st_geometry(tsp), 4326)
zn_bb <- st_bbox(zn_ts)
zn_pts <- st_coordinates(st_cast(zn_ts, "POINT"))
zn_w <- zn_pts[which.min(zn_pts[, "X"]), ]; zn_e <- zn_pts[which.max(zn_pts[, "X"]), ]
zn_lines <- tibble(lon = c(90, 96, 102, 93, 99),
                   type = c(rep("zone boundary", 3), rep("central meridian", 2)))
zn_arrow <- tibble(x = c(99, 93), xend = c(zn_w[["X"]], zn_e[["X"]]),
                   y = c(zn_w[["Y"]], zn_e[["Y"]]) + c(-0.6, 0.6),
                   label = sprintf("%.1f° from %d°E",
                                   abs(c(99, 93) - c(zn_w[["X"]], zn_e[["X"]])), c(99, 93)),
                   col = c("#2171B5", "grey35"))
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = zn_ts, fill = "#fdd0a2", colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(data = zn_lines, aes(xintercept = lon, linetype = type), colour = "grey25") +
  geom_segment(data = zn_arrow, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y, colour = col),
               linewidth = 0.8, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"))) +
  geom_point(data = zn_arrow, aes(x = xend, y = y - c(-0.6, 0.6), colour = col), size = 2) +
  geom_label(data = zn_arrow, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = y + 0.75, label = label, colour = col),
             size = 3.2, label.size = 0, fill = alpha("white", 0.85)) +
  annotate("label", x = c(93, 99), y = 29.6, size = 3.4, linewidth = 0, fill = "white",
           fontface = "bold", label = c("zone 46N\nEPSG:32646", "zone 47N\nEPSG:32647"),
           colour = c("grey35", "#2171B5"), lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("central meridian" = "solid", "zone boundary" = "dashed")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(90, 102, 3), labels = \(x) paste0(x, "°E")) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(89, 103), ylim = c(9.3, 30.4), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Distortion is smallest near the central meridian and increases away from it.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid = element_line(colour = "grey92"))
```

`left_join(pop, by = "TS_PCODE")` joins `pop` to `tsp` in @sec-variables. The MIMU layer and the
OCHA table are shown side by side in @sec-study-area.

## Study area and unit of analysis {#sec-study-area}

The unit of analysis is the township, the third administrative level, after the state or region and
the district. The MIMU layer has 330 townships. Each township has a place code (`TS_PCODE`), and all
330 codes are identical to the codes in the OCHA population table.

::: callout-note
## Administrative levels in Myanmar

| Level | Unit | MIMU field | ACLED field | Count | Place code, Monywa example |
|-------|-----------------|------------|-------------|-------|------------------------------------|
| 1 | State or region | `ST` | `admin1` | 18 | `MMR005` (Sagaing Region) |
| 2 | District | `DT` | `admin2` | 80 | `MMR005D003` (Monywa District) |
| 3 | Township | `TS` | `admin3` | 330 | `MMR005012` (Monywa township) |

ACLED spells eight township names differently from MIMU (@sec-names).

The township code is the code of the state or region followed by a three-digit township number:

<code><span style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">MMR005</span><span style="background: rgba(33, 113, 181, 0.18)">012</span></code> =
<span style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">Sagaing Region</span> + <span style="background: rgba(33, 113, 181, 0.18)">township 012 of Sagaing</span>

The district is not part of the township code. Monywa township is in district `MMR005D003`, and
`D003` does not appear in `MMR005012`.

Myanmar has seven states, seven regions and the Nay Pyi Taw Union Territory, 15 units. MIMU splits
two of the 15 units, each part with its own code:

```{r}
#| label: st-split
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 5.6
sp_st <- tsp |> group_by(ST, ST_PCODE) |> summarise(.groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(piece = if_else(str_detect(ST, "Bago|Shan"), ST, "one value"))
sp_cols <- c("Bago (East)" = "#fdae6b", "Bago (West)" = "#e6550d", "Shan (North)" = "#a1d99b",
             "Shan (South)" = "#41ab5d", "Shan (East)" = "#006d2c", "one value" = "grey88")
sp_xy <- st_coordinates(st_point_on_surface(st_geometry(sp_st))) / 1000   # km
sp_lab <- sp_st |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(x = sp_xy[, 1], y = sp_xy[, 2]) |>
  filter(piece != "one value") |>
  mutate(right = str_detect(ST, "Shan"), lx = if_else(right, 790, -250),
         ly = c(`Bago (West)` = 2060, `Bago (East)` = 1880, `Shan (North)` = 2680,
                `Shan (East)` = 2470, `Shan (South)` = 2260)[ST])
sp_brace <- tibble(x = c(1180, -640), y0 = c(2190, 1810), y1 = c(2750, 2130),
                   tick = c(-20, 20), label = c("Shan:\n3 values", "Bago:\n2 values"),
                   hj = c(0, 1))
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = mutate(sp_st, geometry = geometry / 1000), aes(fill = piece), colour = "white",
          linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(data = sp_lab, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = lx, yend = ly), colour = "grey35",
               linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = sp_lab, aes(x, y), size = 1.2) +
  geom_label(data = sp_lab, aes(lx, ly, label = paste0(ST, "\n", ST_PCODE),
                                hjust = if_else(right, 0, 1)),
             size = 3.2, label.size = 0.15, lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_segment(data = sp_brace, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = y0, yend = y1), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_segment(data = sp_brace, aes(x = x + tick, xend = x, y = y0, yend = y0), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_segment(data = sp_brace, aes(x = x + tick, xend = x, y = y1, yend = y1), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = sp_brace, aes(x - 1.5 * tick, (y0 + y1) / 2, label = label, hjust = hj),
            size = 3.4, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = -1000, y = 1330, hjust = 0, size = 3.3, lineheight = 0.95,
           label = "Grey: the other 13 states and regions,\none value of ST each") +
  annotate("text", x = -1000, y = 1160, hjust = 0, size = 4, fontface = "bold",
           label = "13 + 2 + 3 = 18 values of ST") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sp_cols, guide = "none") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-1010, 1520), ylim = c(1060, 3170), expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11)
```

The three maps below show Myanmar divided into the 18 values of `ST`, the 80 districts and the 330
townships. On each map, the unit that contains Monywa township is shaded, and a circle marks the
location of Monywa township:

```{r}
#| label: admin-levels
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 5.6
lv_st <- tsp |> group_by(ST_PCODE, ST) |> summarise(.groups = "drop")
lv_dt <- tsp |> group_by(DT_PCODE, DT) |> summarise(.groups = "drop")
lv_ts <- filter(tsp, ST == "Sagaing", TS == "Monywa")
lv_focus <- list(filter(lv_st, ST_PCODE == lv_ts$ST_PCODE), filter(lv_dt, DT_PCODE == lv_ts$DT_PCODE),
                 lv_ts)
lv_ring <- st_buffer(st_centroid(st_geometry(lv_ts)), 45000)
lv_panel <- \(units, focus, title, sub) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = units, fill = "grey92", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = focus, aes(fill = "unit that contains Monywa township"), colour = "grey20",
            linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_sf(data = lv_ring, aes(colour = "location of Monywa township"), fill = NA,
            linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = "#fd8d3c", name = NULL) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = "firebrick", name = NULL) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = sub) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), plot.margin = margin(0, 6, 0, 6))
}
lv_panel(lv_st, lv_focus[[1]], paste(nrow(lv_st), "states and regions"),
         paste0("Sagaing\nST_PCODE ", lv_ts$ST_PCODE)) +
  lv_panel(lv_dt, lv_focus[[2]], paste(nrow(lv_dt), "districts"),
           paste0("Monywa District\nDT_PCODE ", lv_ts$DT_PCODE)) +
  lv_panel(tsp, lv_focus[[3]], paste(nrow(tsp), "townships"),
           paste0("Monywa township\nTS_PCODE ", lv_ts$TS_PCODE)) +
  plot_layout(nrow = 1, guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: map-states
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| out-width: "75%"
tmap_mode("plot")
st_bound <- tsp |> group_by(ST) |> summarise()
bb <- st_bbox(tsp)
x0 <- bb[["xmin"]] + 20000; y0 <- bb[["ymin"]] + 30000
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = tsp, aes(fill = ST), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
```

## Study period

The study period is 1 January 2021 to 30 September 2025, 57 months or 19 quarters, set by the
exercise brief and the extent of the ACLED data. The timeline below marks the coup (1 February 2021)
and the start of Operation 1027 (27 October 2023):

- **Military coup, 1 February 2021:** the military removed the elected government (@sec-intro;
  Wikipedia, "Myanmar conflict"). Armed conflict was already recorded in the ethnic states before
  the coup. The first quarter of the study period has one month before the coup and two after it.
- **Operation 1027, 27 October 2023:** a coordinated offensive by "a coalition of three ethnic armed
  groups in Shan State", the Three Brotherhood Alliance of the Arakan Army, the Myanmar National
  Democratic Alliance Army and the Ta'ang National Liberation Army, "named Operation 1027, for the
  date the offensive commenced" (Council on Foreign Relations, 2026; date from Su Mon, 2024). The
  Council on Foreign Relations describes it as "the strongest challenge to military rule since the
  February 2021 coup".
- **Use in the analysis:** the study period is divided at 27 October 2023 into the two phases
  compared in @sec-phases (RQ4). The charts of events and Gi\* over time mark it with a dashed line.

```{r}
#| label: study-timeline
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 2.2
tl_q <- tibble(start = seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2025-07-01"), by = "quarter"),
               label = paste0("Q", quarter(start)))
tl_y <- tibble(year = 2021:2025, start = as.Date(paste0(year, "-01-01")),
               end = pmin(as.Date(paste0(year + 1, "-01-01")), as.Date("2025-10-01")))
tl_ev <- tibble(date = as.Date(c("2021-02-01", "2023-10-27")),
                label = c("Coup\n1 Feb 2021", "Operation 1027\n27 Oct 2023"))
tl_ends <- as.Date(c("2021-01-01", "2025-10-01"))
ggplot() +
  annotate("segment", x = as.Date("2021-01-01"), xend = as.Date("2025-12-20"), y = 0, yend = 0,
           linewidth = 1.3, colour = "grey30", arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"))) +
  annotate("segment", x = c(tl_q$start, tl_ends[2]), y = -0.12, yend = 0.12, colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("segment", x = tl_ends, y = -0.25, yend = 0.25, linewidth = 1.1, colour = "grey15") +
  geom_text(data = tl_q, aes(start + 45, -0.32, label = label), size = 3.2, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_segment(data = tl_y, aes(x = start + 8, xend = end - 8, y = -0.62, yend = -0.62),
               colour = "grey60") +
  geom_text(data = tl_y, aes(start + (end - start) / 2, -0.85, label = year), size = 3.8,
            fontface = "bold") +
  geom_segment(data = tl_ev, aes(x = date, xend = date, y = 0.05, yend = 0.75),
               colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = tl_ev, aes(date, 0), colour = "firebrick", size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(data = tl_ev, aes(date, 1.05, label = label), colour = "firebrick", size = 3.5,
            lineheight = 0.9, hjust = 0.15) +
  annotate("text", x = tl_ends, y = -1.25, label = c("Start: 1 Jan 2021", "End: 30 Sep 2025"),
           size = 3.4, hjust = c(0, 1)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = as.Date(c("2020-12-01", "2026-01-10")), ylim = c(-1.4, 1.45)) +
  theme_void()
```

# Data preparation and quality assessment {#sec-prep}

## Armed conflict events {#sec-event-types}

ACLED codes six event types under three disorder types. The objectives are about violence, so the
analysis variable includes only battles, explosions and remote violence, and violence against
civilians.

```{r}
#| label: event-tree
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3.6
et <- acled |> count(disorder_type, event_type)
et_e <- tibble(event_type = c("Battles", "Explosions/Remote violence", "Violence against civilians",
                              "Riots", "Protests", "Strategic developments"), ye = 6:1) |>
  left_join(count(et, event_type, wt = n, name = "total"), by = "event_type") |>
  mutate(armed = ye >= 4)
et_d <- tibble(disorder_type = c("Political violence", "Demonstrations",
                                 "Political violence; Demonstrations", "Strategic developments"),
               yd = c(5, 2.9, 1.9, 1))
et_l <- et |> left_join(et_d, by = "disorder_type") |> left_join(et_e, by = "event_type")
ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = et_l, aes(x = 1.9, xend = 4.1, y = yd, yend = ye), colour = "grey55",
               linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_label(data = et_l, aes(x = 3, y = yd + (ye - yd) / 2, label = format(n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
             size = 3, label.size = 0, fill = "white") +
  geom_label(data = et_d, aes(x = 1.9, y = yd, label = disorder_type), hjust = 1, size = 3.2,
             fill = "grey95") +
  geom_label(data = et_e, aes(x = 4.1, y = ye, label = paste0(event_type, " (",
             format(total, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), ")"), fill = armed), hjust = 0, size = 3.2) +
  annotate("text", x = c(1.9, 4.1), y = 6.7, label = c("Disorder type", "Event type (events)"),
           hjust = c(1, 0), fontface = "bold", size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#fdd0a2", `FALSE` = "grey95"), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.8, 6.9), ylim = c(0.6, 6.9)) +
  labs(caption = paste("Number on a line: events with that disorder type and that event type.",
                       "Number in brackets: all events of the event type.",
                       "Orange: the three event types in the analysis.", sep = "\n")) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.1))
```

::: callout-note
## ACLED event types

The definitions are from the ACLED Codebook (ACLED, 2023, pp. 11 to 21).

| Event type | What ACLED records | Used here |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------|--------|
| Battles | Violent interaction between two organised armed groups | yes |
| Explosions/Remote violence | Violence by bombs, shelling, airstrikes, drones or landmines, where the target cannot respond | yes |
| Violence against civilians | Violence by an organised armed group against unarmed people | yes |
| Protests | Public demonstration, mostly non-violent | no |
| Riots | Violent demonstration, often unorganised | no |
| Strategic developments | Non-violent events such as troop movements, arrests, agreements and territory transfers | no |

Riots and protests count as demonstrations. The 285 riots and protests that ACLED codes under
political violence are excluded, because ACLED classes these events as demonstrations.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Table

```{r}
#| label: armed
#| echo: false
armed_types <- c("Battles", "Explosions/Remote violence", "Violence against civilians")
armed <- acled |> filter(event_type %in% armed_types)

armed |>
  group_by(event_type) |>
  summarise(events = n(), fatalities = sum(fatalities)) |>
  mutate(`% of events` = 100 * events / sum(events),
         `% of fatalities` = 100 * fatalities / sum(fatalities)) |>
  kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

#### Code

```{r}
#| ref.label: "armed"
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
```
:::

The three armed event types contain `r format(nrow(armed), big.mark = ",")` events
and `r format(sum(armed$fatalities), big.mark = ",")` reported fatalities. Battles
are `r round(100 * mean(armed$event_type == "Battles"))`% of the armed events
and `r round(100 * sum(armed$fatalities[armed$event_type == "Battles"]) / sum(armed$fatalities))`%
of the fatalities.

## Assignment of events to townships {#sec-placement}

Each event is assigned to a township by a point-in-polygon join on its latitude and longitude, after
the points are projected to UTM zone 47N, the projection of the township layer. Coordinate precision
depends on the geo-precision code (@sec-precision).

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Output

```{r}
#| label: project
#| echo: false
pts <- st_as_sf(armed, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(32647)
pts <- st_join(pts, tsp["TS_PCODE"], join = st_intersects)
sum(is.na(pts$TS_PCODE))
```

#### Code

```{r}
#| ref.label: "project"
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
`st_as_sf()` turns the events into points (`remove = FALSE` keeps the coordinate columns for
@sec-outside), `st_transform(32647)` projects them like the townships, and `st_join()` copies the
place code of the township that contains each point, or `NA` if none does.

In the invented example below, points 1 and 2 are inside township A, point 3 is inside township B,
and point 4 is outside townships A and B. `st_join()` returns one row for each point, with the
`TS_PCODE` of the polygon that contains the point, and `NA` for point 4.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 2.6
pj_poly <- tibble(TS_PCODE = c("A", "B"), xmin = c(0.5, 3.5), xmax = c(3.5, 6.5), ymin = 1.5,
                  ymax = 5.5)
pj_pts <- tibble(point = 1:4, x = c(1.4, 2.6, 5, 7.1), y = c(4.3, 2.7, 3.6, 4.6),
                 TS_PCODE = c("A", "A", "B", NA))
pj_tx <- c(10.5, 12.35)                                       # columns of the joined table
pj_cells <- tibble(x = rep(pj_tx, each = 4), y = rep(5:2, 2), w = rep(c(1.5, 2), each = 4),
                   TS_PCODE = rep(pj_pts$TS_PCODE, 2),
                   label = c(pj_pts$point, replace_na(pj_pts$TS_PCODE, "NA")))
pj_head <- tibble(x = pj_tx, y = 6, w = c(1.5, 2), label = c("point", "TS_PCODE"))
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = pj_poly, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
                                fill = TS_PCODE), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = pj_poly, aes((xmin + xmax) / 2, ymin + 0.4, label = paste("Township", TS_PCODE)),
            size = 3.6, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_point(data = pj_pts, aes(x, y), size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(data = pj_pts, aes(x + 0.35, y + 0.35, label = point), size = 3.6) +
  geom_tile(data = bind_rows(pj_cells, pj_head), aes(x, y, width = w, fill = TS_PCODE),
            colour = "white", linewidth = 1, height = 0.95) +
  geom_text(data = pj_cells, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 3.6) +
  geom_text(data = pj_head, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 3.3, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("segment", x = 8.1, xend = 9.6, y = 3.5, yend = 3.5, linewidth = 1.2,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = 8.85, y = 4.1, label = "st_join()", size = 3.7, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 3.9, y = 6.85, label = "Before: points and township polygons", size = 4,
           fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 11.4, y = 6.85, label = "After: one row per point", size = 4,
           fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(A = "#fdd0a2", B = "#c6dbef"), na.value = "grey92",
                    guide = "none") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0.3, 13.6), ylim = c(1.3, 7.2)) +
  theme_void()
```

The table below lists one event, at Muse (MMR10920), after each step. The cells that a step
changes are shaded:

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table class="table table-sm">
<tr><th>after</th><th>object</th><th>columns</th><th>latitude</th><th>longitude</th><th>geometry</th><th>TS_PCODE</th></tr>
<tr><td><code>armed</code> (start)</td><td>table</td><td>31</td><td>23.9933</td><td>97.9103</td><td>none</td><td>none</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>st_as_sf()</code></td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">sf points</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">32</td><td>23.9933</td><td>97.9103</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">POINT (97.9103 23.9933), degrees</td><td>none</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>st_transform(32647)</code></td><td>sf points</td><td>32</td><td>23.9933</td><td>97.9103</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">POINT (389155.2 2653913), metres</td><td>none</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>st_join()</code></td><td>sf points</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">33</td><td>23.9933</td><td>97.9103</td><td>POINT (389155.2 2653913), metres</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">MMR015009 (Muse)</td></tr>
</table>
</div>

`st_as_sf()` keeps longitude and latitude as columns (`remove = FALSE`) and adds `geometry`, a point
with longitude as $x$ and latitude as $y$. `st_join()` returns one row for each of the 54,004
events. Finally, `sum(is.na(pts$TS_PCODE))` counts the events with no township: 12.
:::
:::

Twelve events lie outside every township polygon and have `NA` in `TS_PCODE`. The locations of
the 12 events, and the handling of each, are given in @sec-outside.

### Events outside every township {#sec-outside}

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Table

```{r}
#| label: outside
#| echo: false
pts |>
  filter(is.na(TS_PCODE)) |>
  mutate(dist_km = as.numeric(st_distance(geometry,
           tsp[st_nearest_feature(geometry, tsp), ], by_element = TRUE)) / 1000) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(event_date, event_type, geo_precision, admin3, location, dist_km) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

#### Code

```{r}
#| ref.label: "outside"
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
```
:::

**Rule:** an event within 1 km of a township is assigned to the nearest township, and an event
farther away is dropped. The eight events near a boundary are all within 0.5 km and the four events at
sea are 649 km away, so any threshold between 0.5 km and 649 km gives the same result.

- **Assigned (eight events at five places):** islands and shores simplified in the 1:250,000
  boundaries, and Me Ka Lar on the Thai border. For each of the eight events, the nearest township
  is also the township in its ACLED `admin3` field.
- **Dropped (four events at sea):** ACLED uses "the closest natural location noted in reporting"
  when only a larger region is reported, with geo-precision code 3 (ACLED, 2023, p. 36). Three of
  the four events at the "Bay of Bengal (centroid)" nevertheless have geo-precision code 2.

The first tab shows the six places on maps. The second tab is an interactive map of the 12 events on a
basemap with more detailed coasts and borders than the township layer:

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Each location

```{r}
#| label: outside-zoom
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 6.5
oz_all <- pts |>
  filter(is.na(TS_PCODE)) |>
  mutate(near = st_nearest_feature(geometry, tsp),
         dist_km = as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, tsp[near, ], by_element = TRUE)) / 1000) |>
  add_count(location, name = "n_ev") |>
  group_by(location) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(dist_km > 1, location)
oz_sub <- \(p, ts) sprintf("%.2f km from %s\n%d event%s: %s", p$dist_km, ts$TS, p$n_ev,
                           if (p$n_ev > 1) "s" else "",
                           if (p$dist_km <= 1) "assigned" else "dropped")
oz_keys <- list(
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`nearest township` = "#fdd0a2", `other township` = "grey92",
                               `outside every township` = "white"), name = NULL,
                    limits = c("nearest township", "other township", "outside every township")),
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`event, assigned` = "#2171B5", `event, dropped` = "#CB181D"),
                      name = NULL, limits = c("event, assigned", "event, dropped")),
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`1 km from the township boundary` = "22",
                                   `shortest line from the sea point` = "11"), name = NULL,
                        limits = c("1 km from the township boundary",
                                   "shortest line from the sea point")))
oz_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, lineheight = 1.05),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey70"))
oz_panel <- \(i) {                                         # a place within 1 km of a township
  p <- oz_all[i, ]
  win <- st_bbox(st_buffer(st_geometry(p), 2500))
  ts <- tsp[p$near, ]
  ring <- st_crop(st_boundary(st_buffer(st_geometry(ts), 1000)), win)
  ggplot() +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = win[["xmin"]], xmax = win[["xmax"]], ymin = win[["ymin"]],
                  ymax = win[["ymax"]], fill = "outside every township")) +
    geom_sf(data = st_crop(tsp, win), aes(fill = "other township"), colour = "white") +
    geom_sf(data = st_crop(ts, win), aes(fill = "nearest township"), colour = "grey30") +
    geom_sf(data = ring, aes(linetype = "1 km from the township boundary"), colour = "grey30") +
    geom_sf(data = p, aes(colour = "event, assigned"), size = 2.6) +
    gg_key(win[["xmin"]] + 300, win[["ymin"]] + 350, 5000, km = 1) +
    coord_sf(xlim = win[c(1, 3)], ylim = win[c(2, 4)], datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = p$location, subtitle = oz_sub(p, ts)) +
    oz_keys + oz_theme
}
oz_sea <- \(i) {                                           # the point at sea
  p <- oz_all[i, ]
  ts <- tsp[p$near, ]
  link <- st_nearest_points(st_geometry(p), st_geometry(ts))
  mid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(link))
  win <- st_bbox(st_buffer(st_union(st_geometry(p), st_as_sfc(st_bbox(tsp))), 60000))
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = st_bound, aes(fill = "other township"), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = ts, aes(fill = "nearest township"), colour = "grey30") +
    geom_sf(data = link, aes(linetype = "shortest line from the sea point"), colour = "grey30") +
    geom_sf(data = p, aes(colour = "event, dropped"), size = 2.6) +
    annotate("text", x = mid[1], y = mid[2] + 110000, label = sprintf("%.0f km", p$dist_km),
             size = 3.2) +
    annotate("text", x = st_bbox(ts)[["xmax"]] + 40000, y = st_bbox(ts)[["ymin"]] - 70000,
             label = ts$TS, size = 3, hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey25") +
    gg_key(win[["xmax"]] - 500000, win[["ymin"]] + 160000, 2100000) +
    coord_sf(xlim = win[c(1, 3)], ylim = win[c(2, 4)], datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = p$location, subtitle = oz_sub(p, ts)) +
    oz_keys + oz_theme
}
oz_key <- ggplot(tibble(x = 1:3, y = 1:3)) +                # one shared legend for all panels
  geom_tile(aes(x, y, fill = c("nearest township", "other township", "outside every township")),
            colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(aes(x, y, colour = c("event, assigned", "event, dropped", "event, dropped")),
             size = 2.6) +
  geom_line(aes(x, y, linetype = c(rep("1 km from the township boundary", 2),
                                   "shortest line from the sea point")), colour = "grey30") +
  oz_keys +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1), colour = guide_legend(order = 2),
         linetype = guide_legend(order = 3)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 9.5), legend.key = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
        legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
oz_leg <- gtable::gtable_filter(ggplotGrob(oz_key), "guide-box")
(wrap_plots(c(map(which(oz_all$dist_km <= 1), oz_panel), map(which(oz_all$dist_km > 1), oz_sea)),
            ncol = 3) & theme(legend.position = "none")) /
  wrap_elements(full = oz_leg) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.22))
```

```{r}
om_pts <- pts |>

         dist_km = round(as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, tsp[near, ], by_element = TRUE)) / 1000,
                         2),
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
`oz_panel()` and `oz_sea()` draw one panel per place, with the 1 km line from `st_buffer()` and the
shortest line from the sea point from `st_nearest_points()`. The interactive map is drawn with

### Spatial precision {#sec-precision}

::: callout-note
## ACLED geo-precision codes

ACLED records how precisely each event is located (ACLED, 2023, pp. 35 to 36):

| Code | Location recorded | Armed events |
|------|------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| 1 | The town or village named in the source, at its coordinates | `r format(sum(armed$geo_precision == 1), big.mark = ",")` |
| 2 | A town representing a small area, or a town near which the event occurred | `r format(sum(armed$geo_precision == 2), big.mark = ",")` |
| 3 | A provincial capital or a natural location representing a larger region | `r format(sum(armed$geo_precision == 3), big.mark = ",")` |

A code 3 location can lie in a different township from the event. In the invented example below, one
event occurs in township A. The cross marks where it occurs. The dot marks the
coordinates that ACLED records under each geo-precision code. Under code 3 the coordinates are those
of the state capital in township D, so the point-in-polygon join counts the event in township D.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3
gp_ts <- tibble(ts = c("A", "B", "C", "D"), x = c(0, 4, 0, 4), y = c(4, 4, 0, 0))
gp_codes <- c("Code 1: the village\nnamed in the source", "Code 2: a town\nnear the event",
              "Code 3: the state\ncapital")
gp_rec <- tibble(code = factor(gp_codes, gp_codes), x = c(1.4, 3.1, 5.3), y = c(6.2, 4.9, 1.1),
                 label = c("village", "town", "capital"),
                 counted = c("counted in A", "counted in A", "would be counted in D"),
                 outcome = c("kept", "kept", "excluded"))
gp_cells <- crossing(gp_ts, code = factor(gp_codes, gp_codes)) |>
  left_join(select(gp_rec, code, counted), by = "code") |>
  mutate(hit = ts == str_sub(counted, -1))
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = gp_cells, aes(xmin = x, xmax = x + 4, ymin = y, ymax = y + 4, fill = hit),
            colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = gp_cells, aes(x + 0.45, y + 3.55, label = ts), fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  geom_segment(data = gp_rec, aes(x = 1.4, y = 6.2, xend = x, yend = y), colour = "#08519C",
               linewidth = 0.6, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
  geom_point(data = gp_rec, aes(1.4, 6.2, shape = "where the event occurred",
                                 colour = "where the event occurred"), size = 3.5, stroke = 1.5) +
  geom_point(data = gp_rec, aes(x, y, shape = "the coordinates ACLED records",
                                colour = "the coordinates ACLED records"), size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = gp_rec, aes(x, y - 0.65, label = label), size = 3.2, colour = "#08519C") +
  geom_text(data = gp_rec, aes(4, -0.7, label = paste0(counted, ": ", outcome)), size = 3.2,
            fontface = "bold",
            colour = if_else(gp_rec$outcome == "excluded", "firebrick", "grey15")) +
  geom_rect(data = filter(gp_rec, outcome == "excluded"), aes(xmin = -0.6, xmax = 8.6,
            ymin = -1.25, ymax = 8.25), fill = NA, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`where the event occurred` = 4,
                                `the coordinates ACLED records` = 16), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`where the event occurred` = "firebrick",
                                 `the coordinates ACLED records` = "#08519C"), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ code) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#fdd0a2", `FALSE` = "grey95"), guide = "none") +
  coord_equal(ylim = c(-1.3, 8.3)) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4)),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

Code 3 events are placed at state capitals (the Codebook's provincial capitals) and at natural
locations, for example 15 events at Loikaw, capital of Kayah State, and 8 at Myitkyina, capital of
Kachin State. Counting them in the township of the capital would add events that occurred elsewhere
in the state, so all 94 code 3 events are excluded (0.17% of the armed events).

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Output

```{r}
#| label: clean
#| echo: false
miss <- is.na(pts$TS_PCODE)
near <- st_nearest_feature(pts[miss, ], tsp)
near_km <- as.numeric(st_distance(pts[miss, ], tsp[near, ], by_element = TRUE)) / 1000
pts$TS_PCODE[miss] <- if_else(near_km <= 1, tsp$TS_PCODE[near], NA)

pts <- pts |> filter(!is.na(TS_PCODE), geo_precision < 3)
nrow(pts)
```

#### Code

```{r}
#| ref.label: "clean"
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
The steps below are applied to three rows of `pts`: Muse, which already has a township; an event at the Bay
of Bengal centroid (IOC25), 649 km from any township; and Ma Thay, 0.49 km from Bokpyin. The values
that each step computes are shaded.

**Step 1.** `miss <- is.na(pts$TS_PCODE)` gives one `TRUE` or `FALSE` for each of the 54,004 rows,
`TRUE` for the 12 rows with no township:

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table class="table table-sm">
<tr><th>row</th><th>event_id_cnty</th><th>location</th><th>TS_PCODE</th><th style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">miss</th></tr>
<tr><td>1</td><td>MMR10920</td><td>Muse</td><td>MMR015009</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">FALSE</td></tr>
<tr><td>20,994</td><td>IOC25</td><td>Bay of Bengal (centroid)</td><td>NA</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">TRUE</td></tr>
<tr><td>21,956</td><td>MMR46749</td><td>Ma Thay</td><td>NA</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">TRUE</td></tr>
</table>
</div>

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
↓

`pts[miss, ]` keeps the 12 rows where `miss` is `TRUE`. In `x[rows, columns]`, the blank after the
comma keeps every column.
:::

**Step 2.** `near <- st_nearest_feature(pts[miss, ], tsp)` gives, for each of the 12 events, the row
number of the nearest township in `tsp`:

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table class="table table-sm">
<tr><th>event_id_cnty</th><th>location</th><th style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">near</th><th style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">tsp$TS[near]</th></tr>
<tr><td>IOC25</td><td>Bay of Bengal (centroid)</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">227</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">Cocokyun</td></tr>
<tr><td>MMR46749</td><td>Ma Thay</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">88</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">Bokpyin</td></tr>
</table>
</div>

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
↓

`tsp[near, ]` takes the township rows in the order of `near`, one township for each of the 12
events.
:::

**Step 3.** `near_km` is the distance from each event to its own nearest township.
`by_element = TRUE` pairs the first event with the first township of `tsp[near, ]`, the second with
the second, and so on, in place of all 12 × 12 pairs. `as.numeric()` removes the unit, and dividing
by 1,000 converts metres to kilometres:

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table class="table table-sm">
<tr><th>event_id_cnty</th><th>location</th><th style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">near_km</th></tr>
<tr><td>IOC25</td><td>Bay of Bengal (centroid)</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">649.22</td></tr>
<tr><td>MMR46749</td><td>Ma Thay</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">0.49</td></tr>
</table>
</div>

**Step 4.** `if_else(near_km <= 1, tsp$TS_PCODE[near], NA)` returns the code of the nearest township
where the distance is 1 km or less, and `NA` otherwise:

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table class="table table-sm">
<tr><th>event_id_cnty</th><th>location</th><th style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">near_km <= 1</th><th>tsp$TS_PCODE[near]</th><th style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">result</th></tr>
<tr><td>IOC25</td><td>Bay of Bengal (centroid)</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">FALSE</td><td>MMR013032</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">NA</td></tr>
<tr><td>MMR46749</td><td>Ma Thay</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">TRUE</td><td>MMR006010</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">MMR006010</td></tr>
</table>
</div>

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
↓

`pts$TS_PCODE[miss] <-` writes the 12 results into the 12 rows of `pts` flagged in step 1.
:::

**Step 5.** `filter(!is.na(TS_PCODE), geo_precision < 3)` keeps the rows that have a township and a
geo-precision code of 1 or 2:

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table class="table table-sm">
<tr><th>event_id_cnty</th><th>location</th><th>TS_PCODE</th><th>geo_precision</th><th style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">kept</th></tr>
<tr><td>MMR10920</td><td>Muse</td><td>MMR015009</td><td>2</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">yes</td></tr>
<tr><td>IOC25</td><td>Bay of Bengal (centroid)</td><td>NA</td><td>2</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">no</td></tr>
<tr><td>MMR46749</td><td>Ma Thay</td><td>MMR006010</td><td>2</td><td style="background: rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.30)">yes</td></tr>
</table>
</div>

`filter()` reduces `pts` from 54,004 rows to 53,907. It drops the 4 events at sea, which keep `NA`,
and the 93 placed events with geo-precision code 3. The remaining code 3 event, IOC27, is one of the
4 events at sea.
:::
:::

The cleaned `pts` holds the `r format(nrow(pts), big.mark = ",")` armed events used in the rest of
the analysis.

### Township names {#sec-names}

The `admin3` field of each event was compared with the name of the township polygon that contains
the event.

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Table

```{r}
#| label: names

name_diff <- pts |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(tsp)[, c("TS_PCODE", "TS")], by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  filter(admin3 != TS) |>
  count(admin3, TS, sort = TRUE)
kable(name_diff)

other_township <- c("Kawhmu", "Pekon", "Toungup")   # checked by hand: a different township
n_other <- sum(name_diff$n[name_diff$admin3 %in% other_township])
n_spelling <- sum(name_diff$n) - n_other
n_no_admin3 <- sum(is.na(pts$admin3))
```

#### Code

```{r}
#| ref.label: "names"
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
```
:::

The `admin3` value differs from the polygon name for `r sum(name_diff$n)` events:

- **Same township, different spelling:** the `admin3` value of `r n_spelling` events is a different
  spelling of the polygon name, for example "Dagon Myothit-South" in ACLED and "Dagon Myothit
  (South)" in MIMU.
- **Different township:** the `admin3` value of `r n_other` events names a different township.

A join on names would have lost the `r n_spelling` events with spelling differences and
the `r n_no_admin3` events with no `admin3` value.

### Townships with no armed event

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Table

```{r}
  (\(x) filter(st_drop_geometry(tsp), TS_PCODE %in% x))() |>

  kable()
```

#### Code

```{r}
#| ref.label: "zero"
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
```
:::

No armed event was recorded in eight townships in 57 months:

- **Hopang and Matman districts, northern Shan (four townships):** Mongmao, Pangwaun, Narphan and
  Matman. The United Wa State Army has governed this area since its ceasefire with the military in
  May 1989 (Wikipedia, "Myanmar conflict").
- **Kengtung and Tachileik districts, eastern Shan (three townships):** Mongkhet, Mongla and
  Monghpyak.
- **Cocokyun, Bay of Bengal (one township):** an island group.

A count of zero in these townships may reflect no fighting, limited reporting, or both.

The first tab below has a locator map and one panel for each group. In the interactive map in the
second tab, hovering over a township shows its name, and clicking it shows its state or region,
district, place code and 2023 population.

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Each group

```{r}
#| label: zero-groups
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 7.4
zg_cols <- c("Cocokyun island group" = "#7570b3", "Hopang and Matman districts" = "#1b9e77",
             "Kengtung and Tachileik districts" = "#d95f02")
zg_ts <- tsp |>
  filter(!TS_PCODE %in% pts$TS_PCODE) |>
  mutate(group = case_when(DT %in% c("Hopang", "Matman") ~ "Hopang and Matman districts",
                           DT %in% c("Kengtung", "Tachileik") ~ "Kengtung and Tachileik districts",
                           .default = "Cocokyun island group"))
zg_square <- \(g, pad) {                                   # square window around a group
  bb <- st_bbox(st_buffer(st_union(g), pad))
  h <- max(bb[["xmax"]] - bb[["xmin"]], bb[["ymax"]] - bb[["ymin"]]) / 2
  cx <- mean(bb[c("xmin", "xmax")]); cy <- mean(bb[c("ymin", "ymax")])
  st_bbox(c(xmin = cx - h, ymin = cy - h, xmax = cx + h, ymax = cy + h), crs = st_crs(g))
}
zg_win <- map(names(zg_cols), \(g) zg_square(filter(zg_ts, group == g),
                                              if (g == names(zg_cols)[1]) 8000 else 20000))
zg_rect <- st_sf(group = names(zg_cols), geometry = do.call(c, map(zg_win, st_as_sfc)))
zg_panel <- \(i) {
  g <- names(zg_cols)[i]; win <- zg_win[[i]]; sel <- filter(zg_ts, group == g)
  bar <- if (win[["xmax"]] - win[["xmin"]] > 150000) 50000 else 10000
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = st_crop(tsp, win), fill = "grey92", colour = "white") +
    geom_sf(data = sel, fill = zg_cols[[g]], colour = "grey20", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_label_repel(data = sel, aes(geometry = geometry, label = TS), stat = "sf_coordinates",
                     fun.geometry = st_point_on_surface, size = 3, label.size = 0,
                     fill = alpha("white", 0.85), min.segment.length = 0, seed = 1) +
    gg_key(win[["xmin"]] + bar * 0.15, win[["ymin"]] + 0.08 * (win[["xmax"]] - win[["xmin"]]),
           win[["xmax"]] - win[["xmin"]],
           km = bar / 1000) +
    coord_sf(xlim = win[c(1, 3)], ylim = win[c(2, 4)], datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = sub(" (districts|group)$", "\n\\1", g)) +
    theme_void(base_size = 10) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = zg_cols[[g]], lineheight = 0.9),
          panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey70"))
}
zg_locator <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = tsp, fill = "grey92", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = zg_ts, aes(fill = group), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = zg_rect, aes(colour = group), fill = NA, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = zg_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = zg_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Location of the\nthree groups") +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", lineheight = 0.9))
(zg_locator | zg_panel(2)) / (zg_panel(3) | zg_panel(1)) +
  plot_annotation(caption = paste("North is up in every panel. Boxes on the first map: the extent",
                                  "of each of the other panels."))
```

#### Code

```{r}
#| ref.label: !expr c("zero-groups", "zero-map")
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
`case_when()` groups the townships with no armed event by district, and the interactive map is drawn
as in @sec-outside.
:::

The eight townships stay in every analysis with a count of 0 (@sec-variables), and they appear in
these results:

- **Local statistics (@sec-lmsa):** seven of the eight townships are Low-Low under local Moran's I
  and local Geary's c, and Gi\* cold spots. Local Moran's I has 49 Low-Low townships in all.
  Cocokyun, linked only to Ngapudaw (@sec-weights), is not significant under any local statistic.
- **Emerging hot spot analysis (@sec-ehsa-filter):** before the Mann-Kendall filter, four of the
  eight townships are persistent cold spots and four are sporadic cold spots. The filter removes
  all eight townships.
- **Interpretation (@sec-discussion, @sec-implications):** a cold spot in these townships may come
  from little fighting or from limited reporting.

### Records at each preparation step

```{r}
#| label: record-steps
#| echo: false
fmt <- \(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
n_sea <- sum(miss) - sum(near_km <= 1)
n_placed <- nrow(armed) - n_sea
```

Of the `r fmt(nrow(acled))` records in the ACLED file, `r fmt(nrow(pts))` armed events remain for
the analysis:

| Step | Records kept | Removed | Reason for removal |
|---------------------------------------|----------|----------|--------------------------------------------------|
| ACLED file, 1 Jan 2021 to 30 Sep 2025 | `r fmt(nrow(acled))` | n/a | n/a |
| Armed event types only | `r fmt(nrow(armed))` | `r fmt(nrow(acled) - nrow(armed))` | Protests, riots and strategic developments (@sec-event-types) |
| Events placed in a township | `r fmt(n_placed)` | `r n_sea` | At sea, more than 1 km from every township (@sec-outside) |
| Geo-precision code 1 or 2 | `r fmt(nrow(pts))` | `r n_placed - nrow(pts)` | Coordinates of a state capital or a natural feature (@sec-precision) |

The `r sum(near_km <= 1)` events just outside a township boundary are assigned to the nearest
township (@sec-outside). The analysed events are in `r n_distinct(pts$TS_PCODE)` of
the `r nrow(tsp)` townships.

## Analysis variables {#sec-variables}

```{r}
#| label: counts
#| code-fold: true
counts <- pts |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(TS_PCODE) |>
  summarise(armed = n(),
            battles = sum(event_type == "Battles"),
            remote = sum(event_type == "Explosions/Remote violence"),
            vac = sum(event_type == "Violence against civilians"),
            fatal = sum(fatalities))

tsp <- tsp |>
  left_join(counts, by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  left_join(pop, by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  mutate(across(armed:fatal, \(x) replace_na(x, 0)),
         rate = armed / pop * 1e5)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
`summarise()` counts the events of each type and sums the fatalities in each township. The
`left_join()` calls keep all 330 townships, and `replace_na(x, 0)` gives the eight townships with no
event a count of 0, so that they stay in the analysis.

In the invented example below, five events are in two townships, A and B, and each event type has
its own colour. `summarise()` returns one row for each township. Each count column is the number of
that township's events of one type, and `fatal` is the sum of their fatalities.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4.4
sz_col <- c(B = "#fdd0a2", E = "#c6dbef", V = "#dadaeb")
sz_long <- tibble(TS_PCODE = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B"), type = c("B", "B", "E", "V", "B"),
                  event_type = c("Battles", "Battles", "Explosions/Remote violence",
                                 "Violence against civilians", "Battles"),
                  fatalities = c(2, 0, 1, 4, 0))
sz_lx <- c(1.1, 4.4, 7.7); sz_lw <- c(2.1, 4.4, 2.1)        # columns of the event table
sz_wx <- c(1.1, 3.15, 5.05, 6.95, 8.85, 10.75); sz_ww <- c(2.1, rep(1.8, 5))  # count table
sz_cells <- bind_rows(
  tibble(x = rep(sz_lx, each = 5), y = rep(11:7, 3), w = rep(sz_lw, each = 5),
         type = rep(sz_long$type, 3),
         label = c(sz_long$TS_PCODE, sz_long$event_type, format(sz_long$fatalities))),
  tibble(x = rep(sz_wx, each = 2), y = rep(c(3, 2), 6), w = rep(sz_ww, each = 2),
         type = rep(c(NA, NA, "B", "E", "V", NA), each = 2),
         label = c("A", "B", "3", "2", "2", "1", "1", "0", "0", "1", "3", "4")))
sz_head <- tibble(x = c(sz_lx, sz_wx), y = rep(c(12, 4), c(3, 6)), w = c(sz_lw, sz_ww),
                  type = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "B", "E", "V", NA),
                  label = c("TS_PCODE", "event_type", "fatalities",
                            "TS_PCODE", "armed", "battles", "remote", "vac", "fatal"))
ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = bind_rows(sz_cells, sz_head), aes(x, y, width = w, fill = type),
            colour = "white", linewidth = 1, height = 0.92) +
  geom_text(data = sz_cells, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(data = sz_head, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 3.4, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("segment", x = 4.4, xend = 4.4, y = 6.3, yend = 4.7, linewidth = 1.2,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.9, y = 5.5, label = "group_by(TS_PCODE) |> summarise()", hjust = 0,
           size = 3.6, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.05, y = c(13, 5), hjust = 0, size = 3.9, fontface = "bold",
           label = c("Before: one row per event", "After: one row per township")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sz_col, na.value = "grey92", guide = "none") +
  coord_equal(ratio = 0.62, xlim = c(0, 12), ylim = c(1.4, 13.5), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void()
```
:::

| Variable | Definition | Role |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| `armed` | Armed conflict events, the three event types combined | Main variable for every method |
| `battles`, `remote`, `vac` | Battles; explosions and remote violence; violence against civilians | Comparison of the three event types (@sec-lmsa-types) |
| `fatal` | Reported fatalities | Description only (@sec-fatal) |
| `rate` | `armed` per 100,000 people (2023 projection) | Comparison of the rate pattern with the count pattern (@sec-count-rate) |

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Chart

```{r}
#| label: distribution
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 5
dist_long <- tsp |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(armed, battles, remote, vac) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "events") |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, c("armed", "battles", "remote", "vac"),
                           c("Armed events", "Battles", "Explosions and remote violence",
                             "Violence against civilians")))
dist_mid <- dist_long |>
  summarise(median = median(events), mean = mean(events), .by = variable)

ggplot(dist_long, aes(events)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(data = dist_mid, aes(xintercept = median), colour = "#2171B5", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data = dist_mid, aes(xintercept = mean), colour = "#CB181D", linewidth = 0.9,
             linetype = "22") +
  geom_text(data = dist_mid, aes(Inf, Inf, label = paste("median", median)), vjust = 1.5,
            hjust = 1.05, colour = "#2171B5", size = 3.8) +
  geom_text(data = dist_mid, aes(Inf, Inf, label = paste("mean", round(mean))), vjust = 3.2,
            hjust = 1.05, colour = "#CB181D", size = 3.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "events per township, 2021 to 2025", y = "townships") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

#### Code

```{r}
#| ref.label: "distribution"
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
`pivot_longer()` stacks the four counts so that `facet_wrap()` draws one histogram each, with its
own axes (`scales = "free"`) and the median and mean lines from `dist_mid`.
:::
:::

The counts are right-skewed: in each histogram, the mean is to the right of the median. The median
is `r median(tsp$armed)` armed events per township. The mean is `r round(mean(tsp$armed))`, about
twice the median. A total of `r sum(tsp$armed > 800)` townships have more than 800 armed events. The
choice of LISA labels in @sec-lisa-labels is based on this skew.

## Reported fatalities: zeros and missing figures {#sec-fatal}

- **ACLED rule:** ACLED reports the most conservative fatality figure given by its sources. It
  records zero where the source gives no number (ACLED, 2023, p. 37).
- **Zero fatalities:** `r round(100 * mean(armed$fatalities == 0))`% of the armed events are
  recorded with zero fatalities, including events whose sources reported no number.
- **Use in this report:** fatalities are mapped for description in @sec-geovis. The analysis
  variable is the event count.

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Chart

# Analytical assumptions and methodological decisions {#sec-assumptions}

The results depend on the time bin of the space-time cube, the definition of neighbours, the version
of Gi\* used, and the significance rule.

## Time bin of the space-time cube {#sec-bin}

Emerging hot spot analysis tests each township's series of Gi\* values for a monotonic trend with
the Mann-Kendall test. The test has five data requirements (slides 41 to 43 of the Lesson 5 deck):

| Requirement | Source | In this report |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| No seasonal cycle | Slide 43; Hirsch et al. (1982) | Tested before the bin is chosen: not seasonal under the overall test |
| No covariates | Slide 43; Helsel et al. (2020, p. 336) | No covariate is measured by township and quarter |
| One value per period | Slide 43; Helsel et al. (2020, p. 344) | One count per township per quarter (@sec-cube) |
| At least 8 to 10 periods | Slide 42; Kim and Lee (2023) | 19 quarters |
| No serial correlation | Slide 41; Hamed and Rao (1998) | Not met: most Gi\* series are autocorrelated; corrected test run as a check (@sec-serial) |

- **Seasonal cycle:** the test compares every quarter with every later quarter. A comparison across
  seasons "is really not informative about trend and is more likely to be an expression of the
  differences between seasons" (Helsel et al., 2020, p. 343). Seasonal variation "must be
  compensated for or removed", or "there may be only little power to detect trends which are truly
  present" (p. 342). The Seasonal Kendall test of Hirsch et al. (1982) compares each season only
  with the same season in other years.
- **Covariates:** variables other than time, such as rainfall, "often have considerable influence"
  on a series (Helsel et al., 2020, p. 336). Removing their effect reduces the noise and increases
  the power of the test (p. 336). Population, the only township covariate in this report, is a
  single 2023 value per township (@sec-count-rate), constant across the 19 quarters. The Gi\*
  series are therefore tested without adjustment.
- **Serial correlation:** the emerging hot spot classes on slides 44 and 45 are the classes of the
  ArcGIS emerging hot spot tool. The tool evaluates the trends "using the Mann-Kendall trend test",
  and its documentation describes no correction for serial correlation (Esri, n.d.).
  `emerging_hotspot_analysis()` and In-class Exercise 6 use the same uncorrected test. So do the two
  provided papers that use the ArcGIS tool (Kim and Lee, 2023; Boschan and Roman, 2024). The
  classes in this report use the uncorrected test, which keeps them identical to the definitions on
  slides 44 and 45. The correction of Hamed and Rao (1998) is applied as a check (@sec-serial).

The ACLED events are recorded by day and have to be aggregated to a time bin. The provided papers
use these bins:

| Bin | Papers |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Year | Boschan and Roman (2024); Kim and Lee (2023); Mack and Kam (2018) |
| 6 months | Kim and Lee (2023), for wild boar |
| Month | Tan and Kam (2019) |
| 5 days | Putrenko et al. (2018) |

- **No seasonality test:** no provided paper reports a test for seasonality before choosing the bin.
- **Minimum number of periods:** Kim and Lee (2023) use 6-month bins for wild boar because the
  ArcGIS space-time cube requires at least 10 time periods, close to the 8 to 10 time periods
  recommended on slide 42.
- **Hidden patterns:** Boschan and Roman (2024) suggest that their annual bins may have hidden
  diminishing hot spots.
- **Annual bins:** annual bins would give five periods, fewer than the 8 to 10 periods on slide 42.
  The last period would be nine months long. The candidates are months (57 periods) and quarters (19
  periods).

The three rows below show the study period divided into years, quarters and months, with the share
of township-periods with no armed event for each bin:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 2.2
tb_end <- as.Date("2025-10-01")
tb_bins <- map(c("year", "quarter", "month"), \(u) {
  ev <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(TS_PCODE, start = floor_date(event_date, u))
  starts <- seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), tb_end - 1, by = u)
  tibble(unit = u, start = starts, end = pmin(lead(starts, default = tb_end), tb_end)) |>
    left_join(count(ev, start, wt = n), by = "start") |>
    mutate(zero = 1 - n_distinct(ev$TS_PCODE[ev$start == start]) / nrow(tsp), .by = start)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(row = match(unit, c("month", "quarter", "year")), shade = n / max(n), .by = unit)
tb_lab <- tb_bins |>
  summarise(periods = n(), zero = round(100 * sum(zero) / n()), row = first(row), .by = unit) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(periods, " ", unit, "s\n", zero,
                        "% of township-periods\nwith no armed event"))
ggplot(tb_bins) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = row - 0.38, ymax = row + 0.38, fill = shade),
            colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = tb_lab, aes(as.Date("2025-11-15"), row, label = label), hjust = 0,
            size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2025-04-01"), y = 3.5, label = "last year: 9 months",
           size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2023-05-01"), y = 3.5,
           label = "5 periods, below the 8 to 10 of slide 42", size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey92", high = "#fdae6b", guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(breaks = as.Date(paste0(2021:2025, "-01-01")), date_labels = "%Y",
               expand = expansion(c(0.01, 0))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2027-06-01")), clip = "off") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Darker periods have more armed events, within each row.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
```
